transcript: Meeting header: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (AuroraSearch Head of Search), Priya Singh (AuroraSearch Lead ML Eng), Erin Torres (AuroraSearch PM)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. Demo of API calls, Console ingestion flow, and Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching / quantization. Customer very focused on recall + latency tradeoffs, VPC data controls, and an A/B plan for uplift measurement.
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through the hosted embeddings flow and our reranker pattern, and then show the Console and Optimize recommendations. Ravi will drive the demo.

00:18 Liam: Cool, quick context — we're migrating from an Elastic-backed semantic layer, current infra is on EKS in GCP, and latency targets are ~120ms P95 for query side. Main problem is fetch-time reranking and synonyms causing weird recall drops.

00:35 Ravi: Got it. we'll show how embeddings + a lightweight neural reranker can re-order candidates returned by their existing retriever — so you don't have to rip everything out. Also show how prefix caching and batching can help throughput.
00:50 Erin: Timeline — we're evaluating vendors this month, pilot in April, production in Q2. Security is huge: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 type II, need to show compliance artifacts.
01:05 Maya: We'll share SOC 2 and ISO docs, plus our VPC deployment checklist after the call. we'll also provision a trial API key for your team to run a small benchmark.
01:22 Priya: Awesome. on the reranker side, what's the model footprint? we need something that fits on a cpu or small gpu for dedicated, otherwise cost is killer.

01:30 Ravi: For hosted we run server-side optimized variants — small cross-encoders that can be quantized. In Dedicated/Private you can pin the model variant. Typical approach: use cheap dot-prod for initial candidate scoring (embedding similarity), run a smaller cross-encoder reranker on top for top-K re-rank — usually K=50 or 100 depending on latency budget.
01:56 Liam: And metrics? what's typical recall/precision uplift vs vector-only?

02:02 Ravi: In our benchmarks we see 8–18% NDCG uplift depending on dataset; recall improvements on tail queries particularly strong. Of course depends on your query distribution — we recomend running a small A/B with your query set.
02:20 Maya: We'll help design the A/B and share the sample eval harness we use — it's in the shared folder (link: /redwood/demo/aurorasearch/eval_harness.xlsx)
02:34 (brief crosstalk) Priya: link won't open for me — can you resend? Maya: yes will send after the call.
03:00 --- Demo start ---

03:05 Ravi: I'm going to switch to the Console. First — ingestion: you can upload your corpus or connect via our S3/GCS connectors. Here we show a sample ingestion of docs, automatic chunking and embedding config (512-d default), you can customize chunk size and overlap.

03:31 Ravi: Note: embeddings dimensionality — we support 256/512/1024 depending on model, and we provide normalized and raw vectors. For cosine sim we typically normalize; distance index choices are documented in the console.
03:50 Liam: We use 768 dim today — will there be migration issues?
03:55 Ravi: You can re-embed incrementally, and Redwood supports multi-index strategy during migration so you can run hybrid queries.

04:12 Ravi: Now the API call — here's a simple request: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-512, body: {"text": "..."}. Response includes vector and token counts. then we show a search flow: client sends query embedding, we do ANN search (we use HNSW internally for hosted), return candidates, then call rerank endpoint POST /v1/rerank with top_k candidates and the original query text. The reranker returns scores and the final ordering.
04:50 Priya: Is the reranker run synchronously? we need to know P95 impact.

04:55 Ravi: For hosted, reranker can be synchronous with p95s in the 60–200ms range depending on model size and K. We also have an async rerank option where we return initial results fast and patch results when rerank completes — good for UI UX strategies.
05:20 Erin: That async option might be useful for us, show an example of fallback UX patterns?
05:25 Ravi: Sure — we have sample snippet in the docs. show initial top 10 from vector retrieval then update in the client when rerank payload arrives.

05:40 Maya: Side note on costs — reranking is heavier per-request. Redwood Optimize will recommend tradeoffs like reducing K, batching rerank calls, or quantizing reranker to reduce cost with small accuracy hit.
06:02 Liam: Can you run the reranker on our side (dedicated) to reduce egress concerns?
06:08 Maya: Yes, Dedicated or Private gives control. you can keep everything in your VPC and we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys.
06:20 Priya: How do we measure token costs? we track cost per query and cost per rerank in our budgeting.
06:26 Maya: We'll provide an itemized token and inference cost sheet per model + example traffic profile.
06:40 --- Live example: ingestion + query ---

06:45 Ravi: I'm sending a sample query (timestamped console). you might see a transcription imperf — but result shows initial vector hits then reranked results. Example: original top had an older doc at position 1; reranker pushes down to 6 because recency and semantic match are weaker.
07:10 Priya: That looks promising. does reranker see signals like click priors or recency?

07:15 Ravi: yes you can pass metadata features per doc (click_rate, pub_date) and our reranker model can take those features as side inputs. we show how to pass feature vectors in the rerank payload in the API docs.
07:36 Liam: Security questions — do logs contain query text? how long are logs retained?

07:42 Maya: For hosted we have configurable retention. by default logs are kept 30 days but enterprise customers can opt for custom retention or send logs to their SIEM via webhook. queries are redacted if requested; audit logs for administrative actions are retained per your SLA.
08:05 Priya: And encryption in transit + at rest?
08:07 Maya: TLS in flight; at rest we use AES-256 with customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private via KMS/HSM.
08:20 Erin: Perf — can we run a benchmark using our query set?
08:25 Maya: yes we'll provision a trial key and a quick benchmark script. Ravi will share the script and sample config you can run against hosted endpoints.
08:40 --- Console: Optimize tab ---

08:45 Ravi: here's Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching policy recommendations (batch window 25ms for your QPS), kv cache settings for repeated prefixes, and model selection recommendations (embedding model redwood-embed-512 for cost/quality tradeoff; reranker redwood-rerank-small-3b quantized to int8 for lower cost).
09:10 Liam: Quantization — impact on quality?
09:14 Ravi: small drop in NDCG ~1–3% depending on model and dataset; Optimize simulates expected impact and gives a confidence interval based on prior benchmarks.
09:30 Priya: Can Optimize suggest a rollout plan? we want canary and automatic fallback if quality degrades.

09:35 Ravi: yes the Console supports canary rollouts with automatic metric checks and rollback on NDCG regressions — you provide evaluation prompts and threshold, Console runs traffic split and watches metrics.
09:50 Erin: Great. what's the typical setup effort for a proof-of-concept?

09:55 Maya: Usually 1–2 engineers for a week to run ingestion, basic eval, and a simple UI integration. If you'd like Redwood to support more hands-on, Solutions Eng can assist with an integration pack.
10:10 Liam: Pricing — what's the hosted starting point vs dedicated?

10:15 Maya: Hosted is usage-based per embedding + rerank unit. Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing with monthly commits. i'll send a tailored sheet with example QPS scenarios — that'll include token math for your expected traffic.
10:30 --- Questions from Priya on reranker inputs ---
10:32 Priya: how do you send dense vectors for features? and what's max payload size?

10:37 Ravi: you can include per-doc float arrays, we recommend dimension sizes consistent with embeddings; payload limit for hosted is 2MB per request by default but can be increased for enterprise. We'll note that in the followup.
10:58 Priya: Ok — we'll need info on per-request concurrency limits and connection/fd guidance for high QPS.
11:05 Maya: we'll include connection tuning guidance and recommended client libraries (we have SDKs in Python, Node).
11:20 --- Brief stutter/overlap ---
11:22 Speaker 1 (auto): um sorry small audio artifact, continuing demo
11:30 --- Walkthrough: example rerank payload (pseudo) ---

11:35 Ravi: POST /v1/rerank body: {query: 'best running shoes for flat feet', candidates: [{id:1, score:0.72, metadata:{click:0.03}}, ...], features: {user_tier: 'pro'}} (note: transcript may drop braces), response: reordered list + scores
12:05 Priya: Do you persist rerank outputs? we want a reproducible pipeline for offline eval.
12:10 Ravi: You can run offline reranker via our batch endpoints or run in-house with the same model weights (we provide model binaries for private deployments).
12:28 Liam: For evaluation, will you run the server-side metric collection?
12:32 Ravi: Yes Console can capture per-query metrics if you route eval traffic through our tracing hooks, or you can upload logged results to the eval harness.
12:50 Erin: Any gotchas migrating from Elasticsearch-based BM25 + vectors to this hybrid?

12:55 Ravi: Main points: index format differences, re-embedding cost, and working out K for candidates. we recommend a pilot where you keep BM25 + vectors in parallel for 2 weeks to calibrate thresholds.
13:18 Priya: We'll need help with quality guardrails — sometimes rerankers overfit to queries with exact phrase matches.
13:25 Ravi: We suggest hybrid scoring with a phrase-boost feature so exact matches keep high rank; Optimize can simulate different weights to find balance.
13:40 Maya: Recap — we'll send pricing, SOC2 + ISO docs, VPC checklist, trial API key, ingestion/benchmark script, and the reranker sample recipe.
13:55 Liam: Sounds good. one ask — can you include a sample traffic profile mapping to expected costs?
14:02 Maya: yes will include in the pricing sheet.
14:12 Erin: Next step for us: Priya will share a representative corpus and query set; we'll pick dates for perf run.
14:20 Maya: Thank you all, we'll follow up by EOD with the artifacts. Ravi: anything else?
14:25 Ravi: Just that we'll include the canary rollout example and a short guide on async rerank UX patterns.
14:35 Meeting end
